title: start a full autonomous acceptance and self-healing campaign …
objective:
start a full autonomous acceptance and self-healing campaign for AgenticOS. Test the capabilities one by one, not in parallel. For every test, use the real installed AgenticOS runtime and the physical desktop. If a capability fails or Argus cannot verify it, automatically create a self-heal incident, delegate the repair to AntiGravity, keep the same GoalRun and repair task, diagnose, modify the repository, test, build, deploy, restart if necessary, retry the original command, and let Argus physically verify it. Do not ask me whether you should repair it. Only stop for a genuine external blocker such as authentication or a missing third-party capability.
Test these in order:
1. Open Word and create a genuinely blank document.
2. Take a screenshot and produce a real saved PNG artifact I can open.
3. Open Windows Settings.
4. Open Telegram.
5. Open Adobe.
6. Open Comet Perplexity from the installed/taskbar application.
7. Open Hermes 1 and read fresh visible content from inside it.
8. Open the camera and verify live camera perception.
9. Change the live TTS voice to Zeus authoritative American and verify the actual active provider/voice configuration; if Zeus is not genuinely available, report that as a real blocker instead of pretending it changed.
10. Verify voice responses are not cut off at the last words.
11. Measure and improve speech-end-to-first-audio latency.
12. Verify browser navigation and opening a specific YouTube channel.
For every capability, record the original command, GoalRun ID, incident ID if repair was needed, AntiGravity task ID, files changed, tests, build/deploy evidence, original-command retry, and Argus physical verification. Do not mark a capability PASS from logs alone.
Run only one AntiGravity engineering repair at a time. At the end, show me a capability matrix with PASS, FAILED, or TRUE EXTERNAL BLOCKER.

Relevant Context:
Requested over the JARVIS live conversation channel.
